mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal, or CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tightening labor market, which leads to wage inflation and increased production costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal, or UNRATE < 4% does not correlate with subsequent wage inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals increased demand for housing and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of instances despite positive signal, or HOUST increase does not correlate with broader economic expansion indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal, or INDPRO decrease does not correlate with subsequent economic contraction.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the CPI (CPIAUCSL) is increasing, the combination signals aggressive monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal, or the combination of FEDFUNDS > 4% and increasing CPIAUCSL does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases, it signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite positive signal, or the combination of PAYEMS increase and UNRATE decrease does not correlate with subsequent economic expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real final sales (RSAFS) signals increased consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances despite positive signal, or RSAFS increase does not correlate with broader consumer demand indicators.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) is above its 12-month moving average and GDP (GDPC1) is growing, the combination signals a robust supply side and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite positive signal, or the combination of INDPRO > 12-month MA and GDPC1 growth does not correlate with subsequent economic expansion.
